subject: Social Media
title: Sleep and the Blue Glow
description: A quick, practical guide to Sleep and the Blue Glow.

hook.text: You check Instagram in bed 'for five minutes.' An hour passes. Tomorrow you'll be tired. Tonight you don't care.

buildup.text: Blue light from screens suppresses melatonin by up to 50%. Your brain thinks it's daytime at midnight.

discovery.text: But light isn't the main culprit. Emotional arousal from content keeps the brain alert long after you stop.

twist.text: A boring article won't keep you up. An outrage post will. Platforms serve high-arousal content at night too.

climax.text: Sleep loss compounds. After a week of 6-hour nights, cognition drops as if you'd been awake for 48 hours straight.

punchline.text: The last thing you scroll shapes how you sleep.

quiz.question: What keeps the brain alert more than blue light at bedtime?
